title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.9040: the census production envelope (kappa = 1.0009)

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack of proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.9040 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). This package is aburan28's 312590e9 (125.9054) with only the H1 slowdown allowance changed to kappa = 1.0009; the loops, arrival rows, kernels, table, step price and ledger structure are unchanged. That package builds on bradcush's 87fa94f0 (125.9139) and inherited two pass-2 changes: it stores -(W + T), a member of the same class, so y3' = lambda*(x3 - x_W) + y_W is a fused addition with an unsigned fold and no sign exit; and x3 subtracts x_W and a new table field x_T + 2C0 with both borrow chains ending in ADC, which adds 2p, so its fold is unsigned too: 12,738 instructions per 128 walks and 7,113 per 16, so 99.515625 + 444.5625 counted loop instructions per walk. The arrival pass is unrolled three pairs (six walks) per end test: an arrival remains 30 instructions, a pair adds one LDP of K_cp words and one STP of table addresses, and one TBZ serves six walks, so the arrival row is 31.1667 per walk (the pair count modulo 3 runs a one- or two-pair tail through the same bodies). The round's fixed work, at most 25,109 instructions including the 127 + 15 tail walks, is charged once per round of the one batch of 2^20 walks. h = 0.000203 and p0 = 0.3902033 are unchanged. The ordinary step costs 575.244792 + 25109/2^20 = 575.2687 instructions. kappa = 1.0009 rests on the shipped hazard census at checkpoint period 256: the q29, R = 2^20, dp_bits 5 multi-mode runs give kappa_eff = 1.00000 +- 0.00034 (64 tables) and 0.99993 +- 0.00020 (256 tables), pooled 0.99995 +- 0.00017; pooled over the q29 R = 2^20 runs it is 0.99991 +- 0.00016, and over the eight walk runs 0.99993 +- 0.00015. kappa = 1.0009 is 6.3 pooled standard errors above the eight-run value, 6.0 above the R = 2^20 pool and 5.5 above the dp_bits 5 pool; it is above every R = 2^20 point estimate, and the largest single multi-mode point 1.00109 +- 0.00080 is the R = 2^16 sanity configuration, 0.24 of its own standard error above kappa. The tc runs give walk values 1.0013 +- 0.0034, 1.0013 +- 0.0028 and 0.9949 +- 0.0037; kappa is within 0.12 standard errors of the largest. Rare exits charge 20 milli-units each and run the inline kernel's own instructions; the declared run enters all 383 exit stubs. Recovery probability is greater than 0.39000019 and therefore at least 0.39 (failure rows 1.0103e-7 < 1.1e-7). Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units, charged and included; nonuniform advice is zero. Exact ledger: S_ops = 1.0009*S0 = 2^126.701028, phase 1 = 2^125.903336, hard extras = 2^112.576667, allowance = 2^114.395427, W_ledger = 2^125.9039713 < 2^125.9040; Markov ratio 0.0001918623 < 0.000203; certificate.py checks W^10000 < 1000^10000*2^1259040 and W^10000 > 1000^10000*2^1259039 exactly. No prior acceptance, review verdict or official score is a premise. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk (even-y key, per-trail anchor phases) on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7, with node routing and a long-trail trap test; kernels: Python limb ports of the field kernels against big integers, and the shipped unrolled loops (with their rare exits, on constructed inputs that enter every stub), emitter wrappers and arrival rows executed by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, a bit-exact model and the exact canonical rule, with instruction counts and the ledger of proof.md recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
